name: stakeholders
title: Buying Committee
description: Who is in the deal — every person named or present, their role in the decision judged by an observable quote (economic buyer, champion, blocker), and whether they were on the call or only referenced. Plus a call-level read of single- vs multi-threaded. 'My VP has to approve' is a real receipt; a role you cannot cite is a coverage record, not a claim.
prompt:
Identify every person in the deal — anyone named, referenced, or speaking who has a role in the decision — one entry per person. Do not invent stakeholders; an empty list is correct when only the primary buyer appears and no one else is named.

For each stakeholder:
- evidence: cite the utterance(s) that name or reveal this person, before you write "text". The line that establishes the role_signal below must be among the quotes you cite.
- text: who they are, in the speaker's exact words ("my VP", "our head of ops Priya") — no paraphrase.
- role_signal: their role in the decision, judged by an observable cue in the quote. economic_buyer = holds budget or final approval ("I sign off", "it's my budget", "my VP has to approve" makes the VP the economic_buyer); champion = advocates for the purchase internally ("I'll push for this"); blocker = resists or gatekeeps ("legal won't allow it", "our IT will push back"); influencer = gives input without authority; user = would use the product day to day; unclear = a person is named but their role is not stated. Assign a decision role only when a quote supports it; otherwise "unclear".
- present_on_call: on_call = this person speaks or is directly addressed on the call; referenced = named but not present; unclear.

Then give one call-level `threading` read (single- vs multi-threaded), following the basis rule: basis "cited" needs a quote in evidence; "inferred" is your read with empty evidence; "absent" when the call says nothing about it. single_threaded = only one buyer-side person is in the deal; multi_threaded = two or more buyer-side people are involved (named or present); unclear.

Copy quotes character-for-character, no number-word/digit conversion. When a criterion is not clearly met, use "unclear" over a guess.

`threading.text` is one plain sentence a human reads in the notes (not "Threading: enum"), saying what the threading value means for this deal.
